{'translation': 'The upcoming MacBook Ultra was never going to be cheap, featuring an all-new slim design, OLED display, and touch functionality—even before factoring in price hikes from rising memory costs. The latest reports suggest manufacturing costs could push prices even higher.', 'id': 0}

{'translation': 'Apple has always liked to source components from multiple suppliers to improve display reliability while securing the best prices, and it had hoped to do the same with the MacBook Ultra. However, supply chain sources reveal that Apple has decided to use only one display supplier...', 'id': 1}

{'translation': 'Apple has three display partners across its product lineup: Samsung, LG, and BOE. BOE currently only produces displays for lower-end products, while orders for higher-end displays have consistently been shared between Samsung and LG.', 'id': 2}

{'translation': "The MacBook Ultra will feature Apple's most sophisticated display to date. Combining tandem OLED with touch functionality on the large panels required for laptops is no easy feat, and the latest supply chain reports indicate that Apple has decided to exclusively source these displays from Samsung.", 'id': 3}

{'translation': "According to The Elec, LG failed to meet Apple's required production volumes.", 'id': 4}

{'translation': 'Apple demanded large-scale mass production using large-size substrates. Samsung Display responded with its 8.6th-generation OLED production line, while LG Display reportedly explored options to continue using its existing 6th-generation production line. Although 6th-generation production lines can manufacture laptop OLEDs, substrate efficiency and capacity are both lower than the 8.6th-generation. Due to insufficient initial production volumes, Apple ultimately chose Samsung Display as its sole supplier.', 'id': 5}

{'translation': "It appears LG's production capacity is limited, and the logistical complexity of having two suppliers simply isn't worth it. Outside estimates suggest LG will not be producing displays for this flagship MacBook until at least 2029.", 'id': 6}

{'translation': "This situation clearly puts Samsung in a stronger position in panel price negotiations, which is expected to drive up Apple's manufacturing costs. Apple will most likely pass these expenses on to consumers, just as it has handled rising memory costs.", 'id': 7}

{'translation': "Considering the MacBook Ultra's price could be staggeringly high, how likely are you to consider upgrading? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.", 'id': 8}
